_comment: The components this deployment is made of, and which of them are not
optional. scripts/v2_compose_up.sh reads this file: it is the wrapper's
answer to 'which -f files does a canonical deploy carry', so that answer
lives in the repository instead of in an operator's memory.
Why this file exists: on 2026-08-21 a deploy that ran with only
docker-compose.v2.yml recreated scheduler and worker without
incident evaluator off. Nothing failed and nothing logged it; it was found
by reading schedule_state by hand. On 2026-08-31 the same thing had
happened again and had been true for hours.
`asserts` is the second half of the fix. Naming the file only guarantees
compose was told about it; the assertions are checked against the rendered
configuration *and* against the live container after `up -d`, so a
component that is declared but did not actually reach the process fails
the deploy instead of running silently degraded.
Turning a required component off is a deliberate edit: set its ENABLED
value to "false" in its own compose file and change the assertion here to
match. Dropping the -f flag is no longer a way to do it.

components.name: diagnostic-incidents
components.why: D1: the periodic diagnostic-incident evaluator. Makes no provider call; without it no incident opens or closes, and nothing downstream of incidents (notifications, digests) has anything to say.

components.name: device-status-canary
components.why: M7 Fatia 3's day-plus availability canary. Superseded: docker-compose.v2.yml carries the device-status settings for normal operation since the 2026-08-25 cutover, so layering this file would re-point the poll at the canary's own connection and cap. Listed here to record that it is deliberately not part of a canonical deploy.
